heroHeadline: Day 391: India Protests Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan Elections; IWT 'In Abeyance' Reaffirmed — Ceasefire Holds at Day 391, Bilateral Freeze Comprehensive
heroSubtitle: June 5, 2026: India's MEA lodged a strong formal protest over Pakistan's June 7 Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly elections, reiterating that the entire GB region is an 'integral and inalienable part' of India illegally occupied by Pakistan. In the same press briefing, MEA reaffirmed the Indus Waters Treaty remains 'in abeyance' — rejecting the PCA's May 15 Supplemental Award as 'null and void' — until Pakistan credibly ends cross-border terrorism support. Earlier this week, India also rejected a Kashmir reference in the EU-Pakistan joint communiqué (June 3), while Pakistan's CEC announced GB local elections for August 2 (June 4). The ceasefire holds at Day 391 with no LOC violations since May 10, 2025. Bilateral freeze comprehensive: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT suspended, Pakistan airspace ban through June 23-24, four back-channel contacts the only bilateral interaction. Post-Shangri-La arms race accelerates: Pakistan Fatah-4 cruise missile (750km) operational; both sides plan ~14% defense budget increases for 2026-27 with no arms control framework in place.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
